record.original_question: Can some or all groups of the following sorts be written as homomorphic images of nonprincipal ultraproducts of countable families of groups? This is Question 18 in(G. M. Bergman, Pacific J. Math., 274(2015) 451–495). (a) Infinite finitely generated groups of finite exponent. (b) For an infinite set X, the group of those permutations of X that move only finitely many elements. It is known that no group of permutations containing an element with exactly one infinite orbit can be written as an image of such an ultraproduct(ibid.).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{G_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a countable family of groups and let $\mathcal{U}$ be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$. The ultraproduct $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} G_n$ is defined as the quotient of the direct product $\prod_{n\in\mathbb{N}} G_n$ by the normal subgroup of sequences $(g_n)$ with $\{n : g_n = e\} \in \mathcal{U}$. Call a group $H$ a "countable ultraproduct image" if there exist such a family $\{G_n\}$ and such an ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ together with a surjective homomorphism $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} G_n \twoheadrightarrow H$.

Determine whether each of the following groups is a countable ultraproduct image:

(a) An infinite, finitely generated group $B$ of finite exponent (i.e., there exists $m\ge 1$ with $g^m = e$ for all $g\in B$, and $B$ is generated by finitely many elements but is infinite).

(b) For an infinite set $X$, the finitary symmetric group $\mathrm{FSym}(X)$ consisting of all permutations of $X$ that move only finitely many elements of $X$.

(It is known that no group of permutations of a set that contains an element having exactly one infinite orbit can be a countable ultraproduct image; this rules out the full symmetric group on an infinite set, but does not settle either (a) or (b).)
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint and Journal of Algebra paper "On homomorphic images of ultraproducts" answers several questions of Bergman from his 2015 Pacific J. Math. article, but its scope is limited to questions concerning abelian-image, direct products of finite groups, cotorsion groups, and ultrafilter comparability. It does not address Bergman's Question 18 regarding infinite finitely generated groups of finite exponent or the finitary symmetric group on an infinite set. No published resolution of either part (a) or (b) was located, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: We answer some questions of Bergman regarding homomorphic images of (ultra)products of groups.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work resolves several Bergman questions but not Question 18 about Burnside groups or finitary symmetric groups.
